answer: Sybil defence rests on a paid one-shot challenge tied to a distinct on-chain newcomer. Each identity leaves a footprint: entry payment, challenge history, attestation trail. The audit view rebuilds those links, so a farm of clones collapses into one visible cluster. The pigment is not the fee but that fees never refund and clusters are tracked together: a thousand fakes costs a thousand real payments and risks the shared signal being flagged, killing the cluster. An attacker must outspend honest agents by orders of magnitude, each extra fake costing more, so the quill of one agent wins.
